brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.requirement: A seven-cell honeycomb (centre cell plus six around it)
requirements.evidence: 7 full bases: one at 0,0 and six around it at -1,0, -1,1, 0,-1, 0,1, 1,-1 and 1,0, bolted together with joint bolts.

requirements.requirement: Stands on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: 6 stud spikes facing down at level 0, one at each corner where the centre cell meets two neighbours.

finish.summary: I built a seven-cell honeycomb: one full base in the middle with six full bases around it, all on one storey. It stands on six stud spikes facing down, one at each place where the centre cell meets two of its neighbours. That's twice the three you asked for, and the feet are spread evenly around the middle. I also added 18 solid end caps on the open outer faces and 12 joint bolts so the cells can't slide apart. That makes 31 parts in total, at about 2323 g of filament and 3775 minutes of printing. The final check found no rule problems, and the collision check came back clear.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
